title: Telemetry handoff protocol and backwards-compatibility adapter for SDK/CLI/API
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: We need a predictable, low-friction way for SDKs/CLI/older API clients to send usage telemetry to the console ingestion pipeline while we introduce a new analytics schema (v2). Current approach results in silent parse failures and large post-rollout ingestion spikes when clients start sending unexpected fields.

Goal: Design and implement a 'handoff protocol' + a lightweight backward-compatibility adapter so clients can negotiate schema capabilities and the ingestion pipeline can accept multiple envelope versions without forklift migrations. The solution should: 1) avoid breaking older clients, 2) allow incremental rollout of v2 schema features, 3) make parsing failures observable and auto-fall back to safe paths, and 4) keep per-event overhead minimal.

Proposed design (summary):
- Versioned Envelope: every telemetry POST must include header X-RW-Telemetry-Schema (values: v1, v1.1, v2) and a small capability bitset header X-RW-Telemetry-Caps (comma list of strings).
- Envelope payload shape: {"envelope_version":"v2","event_type":"string","payload":"<opaque JSON>"} (we will publish the exact JSON samples in the spec doc). New fields are introduced under payload.v2 and ingestion performs additive parsing.
- Protocol handshake (optional for heavy clients): a /telemetry/handshake endpoint returns server-supported schema versions and recommended serialization options. SDKs can call this at startup and cache the negotiation result for 24h.
- Backwards-compatibility adapter (service): sidecar adapter running in front of the ingestion cluster that can: 1) translate v2->v1 for legacy parsers when safe, 2) attach a compatibility marker for consumer pipelines to route to fallback decoders, 3) enrich events with derived fields to reduce downstream joins. This adapter also houses the canary routing rules for rollout.
- Incremental rollout plan: use feature-flag-driven routing to send a small percentage (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) of traffic as v2 to new parsers; monitor parsing failures and event-level diffs.
- Failure modes and fallbacks: on schema parse error, adapter will fallback to 'passthrough-v1' mode and emit an alert metric. If adapter receives an unexpected top-level required field in v2, it will drop non-essential fields and mark event with "schema_truncated":true.

Telemetry semantics and engineering tradeoffs:
- We aim for additive-only changes in payload.v2 wherever possible to avoid needing complex transform logic.
- The adapter avoids expensive full-deserialization for simple field extraction by using a streaming JSON scanner for X fields (event_type, client_id, timestamp). This reduces CPU but complicates transform logic for nested v2 structures.
- Handshake adds a small latency at client startup but saves server-initiated errors; optional for embedded/IoT clients.

Observability & metrics to monitor during rollout:
- schema_reject_rate (by client/version)
- adapter_translation_rate and translation_latency
- delta_events_count (v2 vs v1 normalized counts per minute)
- percentage of events marked schema_truncated
- end-to-end ingestion latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)
- downstream analytic regressions (model scoring coverage drop)

Acceptance criteria for full rollout:
- schema_reject_rate < 0.01% for two consecutive days across top 100 clients
- adapter_translation_latency p95 < 200ms under normal load
- no critical downstream dashboards with >5% regression attributed to schema changes

Security & privacy: ensure that adapter preserves PII filtering hooks and that any new fields are evaluated by the sensitive-fields allowlist. The change requires a security review before moving past 25% traffic.

Deliverables:
- Spec doc + sample envelopes (Confluence)
- Handshake endpoint implementation (console-api repo)
- Adapter service with canary routing (telemetry-adapter repo)
- Parser updates in ingestion consumers and test harnesses
- Rollout and rollback runbook (oncall + SRE)
